extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and advanced graduate students in discrete geometry / sphere-packing (readers of Hales's Kepler conjecture proof)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, lemmas, and structural criteria describing the Q-system (a non-overlapping simplex decomposition) and the construction/behavior of V-cells (modified Voronoi cells) used in Hales's proof of the Kepler conjecture. The page gives precise geometric constraints, obstruction rules, and orientation tests used to decide membership/overlap and to bound volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.15 (Incidence relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v, v1, v2, v3, v4 be distinct points in R^3 with pairwise distances at least 2. Suppose that |vi − vj| ≤ 2 t0 for i ≠ j except for the pair {1,4}. Then v does not lie in the convex hull of {v1, v2, v3, v4}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This geometric exclusion lemma is cited from [Hal97a, Lemma 3.5]; used to prevent certain containment/overlap configurations when vertices are sufficiently close pairwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.16 (Vertex outside simplex with short edges)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is a simplex whose edges have length between 2 and 2√(?) (text indicates an upper bound) and v is at distance at least 2 from each vertex of S, then v does not lie in the convex hull of S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses spherical-triangle area bounds: cones over faces of S partition the unit sphere into spherical triangles with edges of arclength ≤ π/2, each area ≤ π/2, leading to contradiction if four such regions covered the sphere. Used to rule out inclusion of distant vertices within a short-edged simplex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 2.17 (No vertex inside quasi-regular tetrahedron/quarter)
rubrics_metrics.description: No vertex of the packing is contained in the convex hull of a quasi-regular tetrahedron or a quarter (other than the simplex's own vertices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate consequence of preceding lemmas (e.g., Lemma 2.16); prevents new packing vertices from lying inside enumerated simplex types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2.18 (Edge 'passes through' a triangle)
rubrics_metrics.description: An edge {v1, v2} passes through triangle {w1, w2, w3} if the convex hull of {v1, v2} meets some point of the convex hull of {w1, w2, w3} and that intersection point is not any of the extreme points v1, v2, w1, w2, w3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalizes intersection notion used throughout to classify how simplices/quasi-regular pieces can interact (edge-through-face vs vertex intersection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.19 (Short edge cannot pass through short triangle)
rubrics_metrics.description: An edge of length ≤ 2 t0 cannot pass through a triangle whose edges have lengths 2 t0, 2 t0, and √8 (or less).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric lower-bound computations show minimal possible length of an edge passing through such a triangle exceeds 2 t0; prevents certain penetration configurations by short edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2.20 (η function = triangle circumradius)
rubrics_metrics.description: η(x,y,z) denotes the circumradius of a triangle with edge-lengths x, y, and z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation used in later lemmas to compare circumradii against thresholds (e.g., 2 or other constants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.21 (Short edge cannot pass through face of small circumradius)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the circumradius of {v1,v2,v3} is less than 2, then an edge {w1,w2} ⊂ Λ of length at most √8 cannot pass through the face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof argues extremal configuration occurs when each |wi − vj| = 2 so that the circumscribed circle lies on sphere radius 2 centered at endpoints; yields a contradiction with length bounds. Prevents diagonals crossing small faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.22 (Endpoints near vertices when diagonal passes through quasi-regular triangle)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an edge of length at most √8 passes through a quasi-regular triangle, then each endpoint of the edge is at distance ≤ 2.2 from each of the triangle's vertices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit proximity bounds (2.2) on endpoints of penetrating diagonals; used to limit possible configurations and to deduce that certain crossings imply quasi-regular tetrahedra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.23 (Adjacency of quasi-regular tetrahedra -> three quarters)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S and S' are quasi-regular tetrahedra sharing a face, and the edge between their two nonshared vertices has length ≤ √8, then the convex hull of S and S' consists of three quarters with diagonal that shared edge; no other quarter overlaps S or S'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines previous proximity/circumradius bounds (Lemma 2.22 and Lemma 2.21) to show the only way two adjacent quasi-regular tetrahedra can appear is as three quarters sharing the diagonal; rules out other overlaps in Q-system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.24 (Endpoints are anchors when diagonal passes through anchored face)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an edge {w1,w2} of length ≤ √8 passes through the face formed by a diagonal {v1,v2} and one of its anchors, then w1 and w2 are also anchors of {v1,v2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses explicit energy/length inequality E(...) > √8 and geometric reasoning to force endpoint anchoring; helpful in anchor-counting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2.25 (Height of a vertex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a saturated packing and fixed coordinates with origin a vertex, the height of a vertex is its distance from the origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple notation used to stratify vertices by radial distance from a chosen origin vertex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2.26 (Enclosed over a figure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A vertex is enclosed over a figure if it lies in the interior of the cone at the origin generated by the figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to describe when a vertex projects into the cone over a face/collection and hence interacts with Q-system elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2.27 (Adjacent pair of quarters; base point and corners)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adjacent pair of quarters consists of two quarters sharing a face along a common diagonal. The common vertex not on the diagonal is the base point; the other four vertices are corners. (Marked distinguished vertices need not coincide with the base point.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial combinatorial object in the Q-system classification; many lemmas consider quarters arranged as adjacent pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2.28 (Conflicting diagonals)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the two corners v and w not on the diagonal satisfy |w−v| < √8, then the base point and four corners can be seen as an adjacent pair in a second way where {v,w} functions as the diagonal; the original diagonal and {v,w} are conflicting diagonals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures when the same 5-point configuration admits two different diagonalizations; used to analyze overlap/anchor structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2.29 (Isolated quarter / isolated pair)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quarter is isolated if it is not part of an adjacent pair. Two isolated quarters that overlap form an isolated pair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification for quarters not belonging to adjacent-pair structures; later lemmas treat isolated quarters specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.30 (Skew quadrilateral with crossing diagonals -> adjacent pair)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four nonzero vertices v1,...,v4 of height ≤ 2 t0 forming a skew quadrilateral whose diagonals {v1,v3} and {v2,v4} have lengths in [2 t0, √8] and cross must be the corners of an adjacent pair of quarters with base point at the origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how local short-distance crossing diagonals yield adjacent-pair geometry; used to locate Q-system elements from vertex configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.31 (Enclosed low vertex over adjacent pair -> quartered octahedron)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Lemma 2.30 hypotheses, if there exists a vertex w of height ≤ √8 enclosed over the adjacent pair, then {0, v1, ..., v4, w} is a quartered octahedron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes when an extra enclosed vertex converts adjacent pairs into a quartered octahedron; uses anchor-distance bounds (Lemma 2.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.32 (Edge passing through both faces forces long length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v1 and v2 be anchors of {0,w} with 2 t0 ≤ |w| ≤ √8. If an edge {v3,v4} passes through both faces {0,w,v1} and {0,w,v2}, then |v3 − v4| > √8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses contraction/stretching and dihedral-angle inequalities (explicit lower bounds like dih(...) > 1.075) to derive contradiction; establishes impossibility of a short edge penetrating both adjacent faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.33 (Restriction on two enclosed vertices over a triangle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two vertices w, w' of height ≤ √8 cannot both be enclosed over a triangle {v1,v2,v3} satisfying |v1−v2| ≤ |v2−v3| ≤ 2 t0, |v1−v3| ≤ 2 t0, and |v2−v3| ≤ 2 t0 (text gives specific inequalities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof analyzes anchor structure and uses Lemma 2.32 to deduce contradiction (|w'| > √8), disallowing multiple enclosed vertices in certain short-triangle cones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.34 (Passing diagonal implies short adjacent edges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v1,v2,v3 be anchors of {0,w} with 2 t0 ≤ |w| ≤ √8 and |v1 − v3| ≤ √8. If {v1,v3} passes through face {0,w,v2} then min(|v1−v2|,|v2−v3|) ≤ 2 t0. Further, if the minimum equals 2 t0, then |v1−v2| = |v2−v3| = 2 t0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigidity/uniqueness argument reduces feasible distances to discrete boundary values; used in anchor-length elimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.35 (Quasi-regular tetrahedron non-overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quasi-regular tetrahedron does not overlap any other simplex in the Q-system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses earlier lemmas excluding edges passing through faces (Lemma 2.19) and adjacency analysis (Lemma 2.23) to show no overlap with enumerated Q-system types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.36 (Quarters in quartered octahedron non-overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quarter in the Q-system that is part of a quartered octahedron does not overlap any other simplex in the Q-system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By construction quarters aligned along different diagonals of an octahedron are excluded from the Q-system; short edges cannot pass through external faces by Lemma 2.19, and diagonals can't pass through external faces by Lemma 2.22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.37 (Strict quarter in adjacent pair doesn't overlap others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Q be a strict quarter that is part of an adjacent pair. If Q belongs to the Q-system, then it does not overlap any other simplex in the Q-system (assuming Q is not part of a quartered octahedron).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed case analysis: overlapping implies diagonals pass through faces and must terminate at vertices; anchor-counting and dihedral-sum inequalities (dih sums) control possibilities. Provides detailed geometric constraints describing exactly how strict quarters could overlap and rules them out for Q-system members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 2.38 (Overlap implies both are adjacent)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a strict quarter Q overlaps a strict quarter that is part of an adjacent pair, then Q is also part of an adjacent pair. Hence if an isolated strict quarter overlaps another strict quarter, both must be isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of the case analysis in Lemma 2.37; used to classify overlapping quarters into adjacent/isolated cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.39 (Isolated overlapping quarter anchor count)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an isolated strict quarter Q overlaps another strict quarter, then the diagonal of Q has exactly three anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed local-geometry description: overlapping isolated pair configuration (Figure 2.3) with six extremal vertices forming an octahedron that is not quartered; shows Q-system excludes such overlapping isolated quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.9 (Q-system simplices do not overlap) — proof summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules defining the Q-system specify a uniquely determined set of simplices and the preceding lemmas show these simplices do not overlap (quasi-regular tetrahedra, quarters in quartered octahedra, quarters in adjacent pairs, and isolated quarters are all treated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesis: the sequence of lemmas (2.35–2.39) exhausts all simplex types in the Q-system and establishes nonoverlap; fundamental structural guarantee for later volume/packing arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.1 (Voronoi cell Ω(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Voronoi cell Ω(v) around a vertex v ∈ Λ is the set of points closer to v than to any other vertex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical Voronoi definition used as background; V-cells will be a modified version respecting barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.2 (Barriers B: which triangles belong)
rubrics_metrics.description: Triangles {v1,v2,v3} with vertices in the packing belong to B (are barriers) iff one or more of: (1) the triangle is quasi-regular; (2) the triangle is a face of a simplex in the Q-system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barriers are the triangular regions that block visibility/assignment in the V-cell construction; later lemmas (e.g., Lemma 3.3) show barriers don't overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.3 (No two barriers overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: No two barriers overlap; i.e., no two open triangular regions of B intersect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses earlier lemmas (2.19, 2.22) to rule out an edge from one triangle passing through another; ensures barrier collection is non-overlapping and suitable for obstruction tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.4 (Obstructed / unobstructed at x)
rubrics_metrics.description: A point y is obstructed at x if the segment from x to y passes through the interior of a triangular region in B. Otherwise y is unobstructed at x. The obstruction relation is symmetric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key notion defining 'line-of-sight' restrictions used in assigning points to V-cells; central to φ and VC definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction detail (Iw cube and R^3(2/3) domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each w∈Λ, Iw is the cube side 4, edges parallel to axes, centered at w (so I0 = { (y1,y2,y3): |yi| ≤ 2^(1/2)? text gives |yi| ≤ 2^(?), but intent: cube of side 4). Define R^3(2/3) as subset of x ∈ R^3 for which x is not equidistant from any two vertices of Λ(x,2/3). Λ(x,2/3) is finite and vertices can be strictly ordered by distance to x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical local domain for φ construction: avoids measure-zero degeneracies (points equidistant to two vertices). The cubes Iw confine V-cells to be reasonably small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.5 (Map φ and set Λx)
rubrics_metrics.description: For x in R^3(2/3), define Λx = { w ∈ Λ : x ∈ Iw and w is unobstructed at x }. If Λx = ∅, let φ(x) be the vertex of Λ(x,2/3) closest to x (Λ saturated ensures nonempty). If Λx nonempty, let φ(x) be the vertex of Λx closest to x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule assigning each generic point x to a closest unobstructed vertex within nearby cube Iw, otherwise to the closest vertex among nearby vertices; core of V-cell assignment. The cube/Iw cutoff prevents remote assignments and pathological behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.6 (V-cell VC(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Λ, VC(v) is defined as the closure of φ^{-1}(v) in R^3; called the V-cell at v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: V-cells partition space (up to boundaries) by the φ rule; V-cells are modified Voronoi cells respecting barriers and cube confinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 3.7 (V-cell containment and cube confinement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a saturated packing, the Voronoi cell at v is contained in a ball centered at v of radius 2, so Iv contains the Voronoi cell. By construction the V-cell at v is confined to cube Iv. The cube choice forces reasonable size for V-cells and avoids assigning distant unobstructed vertices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains motivation for introducing cubes Iw in φ: to avoid remote 'closest unobstructed' pathologies and ensure locality of V-cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.8 (V-cells cover space and have disjoint interiors)
rubrics_metrics.description: V-cells cover R^3; interiors of distinct V-cells are disjoint; each V-cell is the closure of its interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows since φ^{-1}(v) cover R^3(2/3) and closures cover all space; prepares geometric decomposition used in volume/scoring estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.9 (Each V-cell finite union of convex polyhedra)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each V-cell is a finite union of nonoverlapping convex polyhedra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: partition any unit cube E meeting finitely many Iw by perpendicular bisecting planes (for vertex pairs), barrier planes, and planes through triples; finite partition yields convex polyhedral cells whose membership rules are constant on interiors, so each V-cell is finite union of such polyhedra. Important for measure/volume calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 3.10 (V-cells need not be star-convex/convex/connected)
rubrics_metrics.description: V-cells can be nonconvex and even disconnected; hypothetical figure shows V-cell at v could contain points x and z while an intervening point y, closer to another unobstructed vertex w, is not in VC(v), so VC(v) is not star-shaped at v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against assuming simple geometric properties; motivates truncation techniques used later to produce manageable regions for volume bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 3.11 (Truncation and volume estimates)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain explicit lower bounds on volume of V-cells, truncation discards parts of V-cells (e.g., regions where Λx = ∅ or parts not star-shaped). Lemma 3.23 shows inside B(v,t0) the V-cell equals Voronoi cell. Truncation is justified later by scoring function signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: volume contributions in scoring can be bounded by truncating V-cells without losing relevant upper-bound properties due to negative coefficients in scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.12 (Orientation of a simplex face)
rubrics_metrics.description: A face of a simplex has negative orientation if the plane of the face separates the circumcenter of the simplex from the non-face vertex; positive if circumcenter and opposite vertex lie on same side; zero if circumcenter lies in the plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orientation sign is used to decide whether a simplex 'points' into the cone over a face and to detect whether cones/Barriers obstruct Voronoi/V-cell behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.14 (Polynomial χ for orientation test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define polynomial χ(x1,...,x6) = x1 x4 x5 + x1 x6 x4 + x2 x6 x5 + x2 x4 x5 + x5 x3 x6 + x3 x4 x6 − 2 x5 x6 x4 − x1 x2^4 − x3 x2^6 − x2 x2^5 (text formatting condensed); application uses xi = yi^2 where yi are edge lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: χ encodes algebraic test: sign(χ(y1^2,...,y6^2)) determines negative orientation along specified face (Lemma 3.15). Exact polynomial given in the text (use as computational criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.15 (χ-test for negative orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A simplex S(y1,...,y6) has negative orientation along face indexed by (4,5,6) iff χ(y1^2,...,y6^2) < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an explicit algebraic test for orientation: compute χ on squared edge lengths; sign matches orientation via explicit formula t = χ(...) / (positive denominators). Useful for mechanized checking of orientation in constrained domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.16 (Negative orientation with one long edge implies quarter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be a triangle with one edge between pair of vertices of length in [2 t0, √8] and the other two edges of length ≤ 2 t0. If simplex (F, v) has negative orientation along F, then it is a quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monotonicity arguments on χ in variables corresponding to short/long edges reduce sign checks to boundary evaluations; establishes that certain negatively oriented faces must come from quarter simplices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.17 (Negative orientation on quasi-regular triangle -> quasi-regular tetrahedron)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {v1,v2,v3} is a quasi-regular triangle and simplex S = {v, v1,v2,v3} has negative orientation along {v1,v2,v3}, then S is a quasi-regular tetrahedron and |v − vi| < 2 t0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar monotonicity/χ computations as Lemma 3.16; constrains negatively oriented simplices over quasi-regular faces to be small quasi-regular tetrahedra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.18 (Small circumradius implies positive orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a face of a simplex has circumradius less than √2, then the orientation is positive along that face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses monotonicity / algebraic bounds on χ; ensures that faces with small circumradius cannot be negatively oriented, simplifying obstruction/visibility considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.19 (If Voronoi but not V-cell, then lies in cone over a Q0 simplex)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x lies in the open Voronoi cell at the origin but not in the V-cell at origin, then there exists Q ∈ Q0 (simplices in Q-system with vertex at origin) such that x lies in the cone at 0 over Q, and x does not lie in interior of Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: failure to be in VC(0) while still in the Voronoi cell means some barrier blocks assignment; that barrier corresponds to a negatively oriented face of a Q0 simplex, so x lies in its cone. Important for localizing where V-cell and Voronoi differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.20 (Points in B(0,2) not in cones -> origin unobstructed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x lies in the open ball B(0,2) and is not in the closed cone over any simplex in Q0, then the origin is unobstructed at x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that inside radius 2, the only obstructions to the origin come from cones over Q0 simplices; used to prove local coincidence of V-cells and Voronoi cells inside t0-sized balls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3.21 (V-cell contains open unit ball)
rubrics_metrics.description: The V-cell at the origin contains the open unit ball at the origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct consequence of Lemma 3.20 and basic distance geometry; ensures VC(0) includes the immediate neighborhood around the vertex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.22 (Points in B(v,t0) are unobstructed at v)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x ∈ B(v,t0), then x is unobstructed at v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By contradiction using earlier lemmas: any barrier obstructing such an x would force certain distances > t0 contradicting 2 t0 bounds; supports Lemma 3.23 equality of VC and Voronoi on small balls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.23 (VC and Voronoi coincide inside B(v,t0))
rubrics_metrics.description: B(0,t0) ∩ VC(0) = B(0,t0) ∩ Ω(0); inside ball radius t0 the V-cell and Voronoi cell are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines unobstructed results to show local agreement; important for truncation and local volume estimates since Voronoi geometry is simpler near center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.24 (Standard regions on unit sphere via quasi-regular arcs)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every pair v1,v2 such that {0,v1,v2} is quasi-regular, draw a geodesic arc on the unit sphere between radial projections of v1 and v2. These arcs partition the unit sphere into connected components whose closures are standard regions; triangular if bounded by three arcs, otherwise non-triangular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard regions index cones about the origin used to localize simplices and V-cell behavior; later lemmas assert simplices lie in cones over single standard regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.25 (No crossing of certain diagonals / arcs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v1,..,v4 be distinct with |vi| ≤ 2 t0 and diagonals |v1−v3|,|v2−v4| ≤ 2 t0. Then edges {v1,v3} and {v2,v4} do not cross; hence the arcs of Definition 3.24 meet only at endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric bound E(...) contradictions rule out crossing; ensures the geodesic-arc partition on the unit sphere is well-defined (no interior intersections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.26 (Each Q-system simplex at origin lies in cone over some standard region)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each simplex in the Q-system with a vertex at the origin lies entirely in the closed cone over some standard region R (from Definition 3.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids simplices straddling multiple standard-region cones; proof uses nonoverlap of barriers (Lemma 3.3) to preclude sharing of different region cones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark 3.27 (Locality of V-cell membership to cone/region)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x lies in open cone over a Q0 simplex, Lemma 3.28 (not in this chunk) describes VC decomposition inside that simplex. If x lies in open cone over a standard region R but not in cone over any Q-simplex, Lemma 3.29 (not in this chunk) states: for unobstructed x, membership in VC(0) can be decided by considering only vertices w that lie in the closed cone over R. Thus intersection of a V-cell with cone over R is local.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that V-cell assignment is local within cones determined by standard regions or Q0 simplices; motivates subsequent lemmas to restrict attention to finite local vertex sets when analyzing V-cells.
